consequences: Long-run admission converges to limitPerSec with at most one initial burst window; idleness restores at most burst capacity; zero rate or zero burst admits nothing. Client-side only; no server enforcement is asserted. Time complexity O(1) amortized per check (eviction amortized O(1)); space O(burst) for timestamps plus O(1) credit state.
context: Issue #102 evidence confirmed: both TS and Rust RateLimiter.check admitted purely by rolling-window count vs burst; limitPerSec/limit_per_sec was unused (TS) or explicitly discarded (Rust let _ =). Canonical ipc-agent-rfc.md (bitty-docs fc7ed97) L367-374 and devtools-rfc.md L498-500 define RC-9 as 100 req/s sustained with 2x burst for 1s and require tests to parameterize on declared values.
decision_body: Keep the rolling burst-window cap and its timestamp FIFO exactly as-is; add per-request refill credit of elapsedMs*limitPerSec (elapsed measured in caller-supplied virtual monotonic milliseconds, clamped against regressions) capped at burst*RC9_WINDOW_MS, and require one window-worth of credit per admission. No new configuration surface or policy constants; existing RC9_REQ_PER_SEC/RC9_BURST_PER_SEC/RC9_WINDOW_MS are the only inputs. Implemented identically in src/transport.ts and crates/devtools-client/src/transport.rs with benign in-memory virtual-clock model tests in tests/transport.test.ts and the Rust test module.
rationale: Implements the documented sustained refill with bounded burst without inventing a new policy number, keeps admission semantics monotonic under clock regression, and leaves reconnect-count work (#106/CTX-0056) untouched. Credit is bounded so idle time can never exceed the 2x burst ceiling.
title: CTX-0055: implement sustained refill as millisecond token credit derived from existing RC-9 constants
